conventions.convention: The binary adjacency matrix is over F₂ = Z/2Z, in fixed vertex order, symmetric with zero diagonal; the empty graph has the unique 0×0 matrix.
J(α) = H diag(1,e^{iα}), and the outcome-b measurement vector is J(α)†|b⟩. The scalar phase of J is fixed.
The graph-state register follows fixed vertex order; each CZ is diag(1,1,1,−1), and the defining edge product is lexicographic. The empty graph state is 1 in C.
Schedule wire j denotes source circuit wire j−1. Each round applies its CZ matching before its J gates. Mixed-layer padding contributes e^{iπ(n−|J_r|)/4} to σ_C.

A pattern permits overlapping input and output sets. Complementary input vertices receive |+⟩; measured vertices are removed in the specified measurement order, while outputs retain inherited vertex order. Raw branch maps exclude terminal corrections.
The frame is X^xZ^z. The adaptive angle is (−1)^xβ, the new frame is (b⊕z,x), and its scalar is 1 for x=0 and (−1)^z e^{−iβ} for x=1.

Transport vertices are ordered wire first, then column; measurements are ordered round first, then wire. The terminal correction is P(x^R,z^R)†, and λ includes both the padding phase and matching signs.
Conditional states exist only on positive-probability branches; a zero-probability branch has zero unnormalized output and no normalized conditional output.

Exact synthesis uses instance-specific exact gate matrices, with no finite-bit encoding or decomposition-time guarantee. For zero qubits only the unitary channel, rather than an arbitrary scalar unitary matrix, is represented by the empty circuit.

load_bearing.statement: The outcome-b branch operator is K_b = 2^{−1/2}X^bJ(α). Each outcome has probability 1/2, and the operator identity also holds with a finite-dimensional reference register.

For the encoded finite n-wire J/CZ circuit, every transcript has K_b = 2^{−nR/2}λ_b P_b U_C, with the encoding's exact unit-modulus λ_b. Every transcript has probability 2^{−nR}, and the corrected branches sum to the channel ρ ↦ U_CρU_C†.

For every finite adaptive pattern, pure-input branch probabilities are squared branch-map norms, mixed-input probabilities are tr(K_bρK_b†), and their sum is one. Zero-probability transcripts have no normalized conditional output.
For n ≥ 0 and a matching M, CZ_M P(x,z) = (−1)^{q_M(x)}P(x,z⊕A_Mx)CZ_M, with the stated empty-register convention.
For a circuit C as in the normalized transport schedule, the chronological product of the normalized rounds satisfies Ũ_C = σ_C U_C.

For every n ≥ 1 and U ∈ U(2^n), there is a finite exact n-wire circuit without ancillas, using arbitrary one-qubit gates and CNOT gates, whose denotation is exactly U. For n=0 the unitary channel is represented by the empty circuit.
A multiplexed y- or z-axis rotation with k controls has an exact circuit on the same k+1 wires without ancillas: one rotation and no CNOT for k=0, and 2^k target rotations and 2^k CNOTs for k>0.

Every finite open-graph adaptive pattern has a raw measurement circuit with exactly its raw branch operators, probabilities and positive-probability conditional outputs. Appending its specified, separately charged correction suffix gives exactly its corrected branch operators and instrument.
The operators K_v = X_v∏_{u∈N(v)}Z_u are commuting Hermitian involutions fixing |G⟩, with independent binary Pauli labels, including the empty generating family.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite, unordered, distinct-endpoint edge sets in graph-state and transport constructions.
The order-two field convention for binary adjacency matrices.
Vector-space interpretation of binary coordinate and frame vectors.
Binary adjacency matrices, including the unique empty matrix.
Basis-independent trace and its zero-dimensional convention in branch calculations.
Rectangular trace cyclicity in branch normalization, isometric preparation and instrument completeness.
Root-linear-first coordinate pairing and the identity tr(uu†)=‖u‖².
Exact real arguments for diagonal unitary entries and cosine-sine rotation angles.
Nonnegative spectral eigenvalues and the implication that a nonnegative trace-zero branch operator is zero.
Input-independent transcript probabilities under unitary conjugation.

concerns.concern: The Definition opens 'Let C be a finite n-wire circuit' without explicitly restricting its alphabet to J and CZ, although its title and the preservation lemma's Given impose that intended restriction. Its cases otherwise ignore unsupported gates: a one-wire X-only layer has J_r=M_r=∅ and produces no rounds. State the J/CZ input restriction explicitly so the Definition and preservation Statement have the same domain.

The item has kind: definition and a def- ID, but its defining content is an operational procedure: 'Start with σ_C=1 and process the original layers in order', followed by four branches that append rounds and update σ_C. This needs reconciliation with the dispatch's requirement that procedures use kind: algorithm and an alg- ID, while also preserving the established item ID.

The item has kind: definition and a def- ID, but specifies a circuit-to-pattern construction with initialization, round-by-round frame updates, angle selection and terminal correction. Its procedural classification needs reconciliation with the dispatch's algorithm rule and established-ID preservation requirement.

seams_checked.note: This declared prerequisite supplies context, but no assigned item cites a Bell-protocol result. One-bit teleportation is proved locally; its single-bit outcome convention does not import or reverse the Bell protocol's phase/flip labels.

The uses retain chronological right-to-left matrix products, disjoint layer supports, ordered local embeddings and separately charged suffix access. The zero-based source wires are explicitly translated to schedule indices.

The CSD, two-block demultiplexing, three-CNOT base case and Euler interfaces are used with their exact phases. The local QSD theorem asserts finite existence without importing optimized gate counts or bit-complexity guarantees.
CZ is the exact angle-π controlled phase and CNOT retains control-target order. No controlled access is inferred from an arbitrary unitary matrix.
Bras are linear functionals obtained from the root-linear-first pairing; outer products use coordinate matrices xy†. Measurement contractions and norm-square probabilities respect this convention.

Projective bases are complete, branch maps are shown completely positive, normalization is proved, and conditional outputs are assigned only at positive probability. No conditional instrument is inferred from a POVM alone.
The frame order X^xZ^z and binary label order (x,z) are retained. Matching signs and adaptive phases are explicit; the n≥1 Pauli definition is extended locally and explicitly for n=0.
Pure states are rays and density operators are nonnegative trace-one operators on nonzero spaces. The zero-qubit space is C, so the state hypotheses remain satisfied.
H, X, Y, Z and the negative-exponent rotation convention agree with the suppliers. The opposite-sign Euler notation is expressly local and translated back to the supplier's angles.

Ordered tensor factors, big-endian bitstrings, tensor contractions and wire permutations retain the supplier conventions. Empty registers are C, and the input/output orders of the transport graph match source wire order.

The graph generators are first shown to generate a stabilizer subgroup excluding −I, with rank n. The group-average projector and 2^{n−r} code-dimension results then apply with their stated hypotheses; n=0 is handled separately.
